History and Physical (H&P – Detailed)

Consult Summary:
• 26-year-old female with 2-day history of central lower-abdominal pain, mild urinary frequency, and pink-tinged urine; clinically treated as an uncomplicated urinary tract infection (UTI) with a 3-day antibiotic course.

History:
• Presenting complaint – lower-abdominal (“lower tummy”) pain for 2 days.  
• Character/location – central, non-radiating.  
• Associated symptoms – feeling “hot and sweaty,” subjective nausea without vomiting, mild ↑ urinary frequency, thirst, pink-tinged urine noted once.  
• Denies – dysuria, flank/back pain, vaginal discharge, abnormal per-vaginal bleeding, acid reflux, recent travel, prior similar episodes.  
• Bowel habit – constipated last week, now normal; last bowel movement 2 h ago, normal, no blood.  
• Temperature – self-checked once 1 h prior: 37 °C; no recorded fevers.  
• Review of systems otherwise non-contributory.

Past Medical History:
• No chronic medical conditions reported.

Medications:
• None reported (no regular or OTC medications).  
• Previous contraceptive implant removed 1 yr ago.  
Allergies:
• Amoxicillin – reaction details not documented.

Social History:
• Lives with parents.  
• Non-smoker.  
• Alcohol: ~1 beer, 4×/week.  
• No substance use reported.

Family History:
• Mother – early breast cancer, treated.  
• No other significant familial illnesses mentioned.

Physical Examination:
• Vitals: Patient-reported temperature 37 °C; other vitals not documented.  
• No in-person physical examination performed (telehealth consultation).

Investigations:
• None performed or available at time of consult.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1 – Suspected uncomplicated urinary tract infection presenting with lower-abdominal pain, mild urinary frequency, and hematuria.
  • Plan:
    – Prescribe 3-day course of oral antibiotic (specific agent/dose/route/frequency not documented; to be sent to patient’s nominated pharmacy).  
    – Begin medication immediately upon collection; take twice daily for 3 days.  
    – Safety-net advice: seek urgent review if pain worsens, fever develops, back/flank pain appears, or any new symptoms arise; consult again if recurrence occurs.  
    – Consider face-to-face examination and urinalysis if no improvement or symptoms escalate.

General Plan items:
  • None additional.

Quality checks:
• Missing but expected: complete vitals, urinalysis, pregnancy status, detailed antibiotic name/dose, reaction specifics for amoxicillin allergy.  
• Internal conflicts: none identified.  
• Transcript quality: intermittent inaudible segments; core clinical data obtainable but some details (e.g., exact age, allergy reaction) absent.
